stem: During pre-transplant education, a kidney candidate asks why immunosuppressive medications must be taken every day even when they feel well. Which response BEST reflects the core teaching point a coordinator should reinforce?

options.text: Missing doses mainly increases cosmetic side effects but does not change rejection risk.
Therapeutic drug levels depend on consistent dosing; skipped doses can allow rejection before symptoms appear.
Immunosuppression is needed only during the first month after transplant.
Doses can be stopped whenever infection symptoms resolve without notifying the team.

explanation.rationale_correct: Maintenance immunosuppression prevents subclinical rejection that can progress to graft injury before the recipient feels ill. Coordinators emphasize adherence, trough monitoring when ordered, and contacting the team before changing doses.

rationale_incorrect.A: Nonadherence raises rejection and infection risk; it is not limited to cosmetic effects.
rationale_incorrect.C: Lifelong immunosuppression is required for most solid-organ recipients unless a specific research or medical exception applies.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients should not independently stop immunosuppression; infection management requires coordinated dose adjustments.

references.citation: AST/ASTS Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of the Kidney Transplant Recipient (patient education and immunosuppression adherence).

notes: Reviewer: confirm current AST guideline citation and add a verified public URL if available before promoting to reviewed.

stem: A liver transplant recipient completed education two weeks ago. Today they report oral white patches, fever to 38.3°C (101°F), and fatigue but deny cough or dysuria. Which instruction is MOST appropriate for the coordinator to give before the clinic team reviews the case?

options.text: Stop all immunosuppression until the fever resolves.
Continue prescribed medications, avoid live vaccines, and contact the transplant team today for same-day guidance.
Treat with leftover oral antibiotics from a prior prescription without reporting symptoms.
Wait one week unless temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F).

explanation.rationale_correct: Fever and mucosal changes in an immunosuppressed recipient warrant prompt team contact because infection and rejection can present subtly. Education stresses early reporting, medication continuity unless directed otherwise, and infection-prevention practices.

rationale_incorrect.A: Stopping immunosuppression without medical direction can trigger rejection and is not appropriate first-line advice.
rationale_incorrect.C: Using unprescribed antibiotics delays proper evaluation and may mask culture data.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppressed recipients are taught to report fever early rather than waiting for extreme temperatures.

references.citation: CDC Guidelines for Preventing Opportunistic Infections Among Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients (infection prevention principles applicable to solid-organ immunosuppression education).

notes: Reviewer: verify whether a more current CDC solid-organ transplant patient-education source should be cited instead of this MMWR reference.

stem: A potential living kidney donor asks whether donation guarantees a transplant for their intended recipient. Which explanation is MOST accurate for the coordinator to provide?

options.text: Living donation automatically moves the intended recipient to the top of every national deceased-donor list.
Directed donation can proceed when immunologic compatibility and program criteria are met, but listing and allocation rules still apply to other candidates.
Living donors are evaluated only for blood type and do not require medical or psychosocial clearance.
Recipients never need additional testing once a living donor volunteers.

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donation education clarifies that donors undergo full independent evaluation, compatibility must be confirmed, and program/OPTN policies govern how organs are allocated even in directed donation scenarios.

rationale_incorrect.A: Directed living donation does not grant automatic priority on unrelated deceased-donor allocation pathways.
rationale_incorrect.C: Living donors require comprehensive medical, surgical, and psychosocial evaluation beyond ABO typing.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients still need updated testing and clearance before transplant can proceed.

references.citation: OPTN Policies — living donor requirements and allocation principles.

notes: Reviewer: replace base URL with verified deep links to current OPTN living-donor policy sections before promoting to reviewed.
